statement: x06.1's append-only observation/graph-event log reuses enforcer_core::telemetry::RunTelemetrySink and verify_file_chain (the d04 primitive) instead of hand-rolling a new hash-chain writer: the .chain sidecar is written as an INDEPENDENT file from the data line, so verification compares the data file against that independently-persisted sidecar rather than recomputing an 'expected' digest from the same file being checked.
why: L37 flags exactly this failure mode by name: d04's own first attempt at chain verify was vacuous (self-referential) and was only caught by a seeded tampering test. Reusing the already-tampering-tested d04 primitive instead of writing a second, unproven chain implementation avoids repeating that mistake and keeps one audited hash-chain code path in the workspace instead of two.
howToApply: Any new append-only/tamper-evident log in this workspace should be built on enforcer_core::telemetry::RunTelemetrySink + verify_file_chain (or enforcer_core::hash_chain directly for a bespoke shape), and MUST ship a tampering test that mutates the data file while leaving the .chain sidecar untouched, then asserts verification fails closed -- never a test that only checks the happy path.

statement: x06.1 does NOT link the real `duckdb` crate by default. The analytics read model is a trait (store::analytics::AnalyticsReadModel) with a dependency-free, deterministic in-process aggregator (InProcessAnalytics) as the default backend; real DuckDB is wired behind an opt-in `duckdb-analytics` Cargo feature that is not exercised by this lane's gate.
why: The duckdb crate's bundled feature compiles DuckDB's C++ amalgamation from source, which is a heavy, historically-unreliable build on this workspace's Windows toolchain with no cached-artifact story in this repo's CI. Making it a default dependency of enforcer-memory would make the crate's own build flaky on the exact platform x06 targets first -- the opposite of the owner-intent doc's 'local-first, mechanically testable' requirement. The owner-intent fake-green definition explicitly forbids claiming a capability (real DuckDB) the gate never actually compiles or runs.
howToApply: When a subpack's hard requirement names a heavyweight/optional native dependency and the subpack text itself offers a fallback escape hatch, take the escape hatch and record the decision in the crate's module doc (not just a commit message) so a future worker who wires the real backend can find the exact reasoning and the seam it must satisfy (AnalyticsReadModel here) instead of re-deciding from scratch.

evidence.ref: docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_IMPLEMENTATION_PACKS.md X06.1 hard requirements; crates/enforcer-memory/src/store/analytics.rs module doc (DuckDB decision record)

statement: Store::open on a project directory with no store.json marker returns MemoryError::UnknownProject and creates NOTHING on disk (no directory, no file); only Store::init may create a project's store, and it is idempotent. The project id itself is a deterministic hash of the NORMALIZED repo root, so C:\Projects\x and C:/Projects/x resolve to the identical store directory.
why: The subpack's 'no ghost project database creation' hard requirement plus the owner-intent doc's local-first/deterministic mandate together rule out the common convenience pattern of open-or-create for a per-project store: a typo'd or stale repo-root argument must fail loudly, not silently spin up an empty database that later looks like real (empty) history.
howToApply: Any per-project or per-repo store/cache in this workspace should split its lifecycle into an explicit init (create, idempotent) and a strict open (read-only existence check, never creates), and should key its on-disk location off a value derived from enforcer_domain::paths normalization so Windows-backslash and POSIX-forward-slash spellings of the same root are provably the same project -- see the windows_backslash_and_posix_forward_slash_roots_map_to_the_same_store test for the mechanical proof shape.
